agent_notes: The signature change `post(url: string)` to `post(url: string, body?: object)` is backward compatible. The new parameter is optional, and `body ?? null` sends exactly what the old code sent when no body is given.
There are 4 existing callers and all pass no body, so their behavior does not change: model-file.service.ts:61, 74 and 87, and server-command.service.ts:26.
MockRestService (tests/mocks/mock-rest.service.ts) only stubs `sendRequest` and never stubbed `post`, so no test mock needs updating.

When `body` is a plain object, Angular HttpClient serializes it to JSON and sets `Content-Type: application/json`. That matches what the backend expects, since `__handle_set_config` reads `bottle.request.json`, and bottle returns None for `request.json` when the Content-Type is not JSON.

The `object` type also accepts arrays, class instances and Blob/FormData, and HttpClient serializes those differently, for example FormData goes out as multipart. No current caller passes one of these, so this is only a theoretical concern for the future. `Record<string, unknown>` would be a tighter type.
Caching is unchanged. `shareReplay(1)` is still applied to each call, and each call builds a new observable, so different bodies cannot share a cached response.
This diff has no database, schema or migration effects. It has no performance effect, since the only cost is serializing a small JSON body.
Blast radius of the changed lines: one method in RestService and 4 existing callers whose behavior is unchanged. Risk is very low.

The real risk is outside this diff. At HEAD, the backend accepts only POST on /server/config/set, but ConfigService still sends GET requests with the values in the URL path, so settings saves are broken until the frontend migration lands. See impact-1.
Verdict: this diff can ship as-is. Do not release phase 111 until ConfigService uses the new `post(url, body)`.
